text: can you explain gradient descent in 3d surface

Given: Loss surface: f(x,y)=x^2+2y^2, Minimum of the surface: (x,y,z)=(0,0,0), Illustrative starting point: (x_0,y_0)=(3,2), Fixed learning rate: eta=0.1, Gradient returned by symbolic differentiation: ∇f(x,y)=(2x,4y)
Find: The successive points generated by gradient descent and the reason they converge toward the minimum

1. Identify the surface and its minimum
   z=f(x,y)=x²+2y²
   The height z is the loss. Since x^2≥0 and 2y^2≥0, the smallest possible height is reached when x=0 and y=0. Therefore the minimum point is (0,0,0).

2. Choose a concrete starting point
   (x₀,y₀)=(3,2)
   To make the visual path concrete, begin at the point (3,2) in the xy-plane. The corresponding surface height is obtained by substituting this point into the given loss function.

3. Compute the gradient
   ∇ f(x,y)=begin bmatrix2x\\4yend bmatrix
   The gradient consists of the partial derivatives of the loss with respect to x and y. Symbolic differentiation gives the components 2x and 4y. This vector points uphill on the surface.

4. Reverse the gradient to move downhill
   -∇ f(x,y)=begin bmatrix-2x\\-4yend bmatrix
   Because the gradient points in the direction of greatest local increase, its negative points in the direction of greatest local decrease. The visualization should show this arrow in the xy-plane, attached to the current point on the 3D surface.

5. Apply the gradient-descent update rule
   (xₖ₊₁,yₖ₊₁)=(xₖ,yₖ)-η∇ f(xₖ,yₖ)
   At each iteration, multiply the gradient at the current point by the learning rate eta and subtract the result from the current coordinates. With eta=0.1, this gives the concrete coordinate updates x_{k+1}=x_k-0.1(2x_k) and y_{k+1}=y_k-0.1(4y_k).

6. Calculate the first descent step
   (x₁,y₁)=(3-0.1(2·3), 2-0.1(4·2))=(2.4,1.2)
   At (3,2), the gradient is (6,8). The negative-gradient step therefore moves left in x and downward in y, producing the next point (2.4,1.2). The corresponding point on the surface is lower than the starting point.

7. Generate the sequence of points
   x: 3, 2.4, 1.92, 1.536, 1.2288, 0.98304
   Repeated numerical iteration of the x-update produces the displayed trajectory. The x-coordinate moves toward zero without changing sign.

8. Generate the y-coordinate sequence
   y: 2, 1.2, 0.72, 0.432, 0.2592, 0.15552
   Repeated numerical iteration of the y-update produces the displayed trajectory. The y-coordinate also moves toward zero, and it decreases faster than x because the loss is steeper in the y-direction.

9. Check that one update lowers the loss
   f(x-0.1(2x),y-0.1(4y))=0.64x²+0.72y²
   After one update, the loss becomes 0.64x^2+0.72y^2. Both coefficients are smaller than the corresponding original coefficients 1 and 2, so for any nonzero point the loss decreases under this particular learning rate.

10. Describe convergence toward the minimum
   lim ₖ→∞(xₖ,yₖ)=(0,0)
   The numerical sequences show both coordinates shrinking toward zero. Consequently, the plotted points approach the unique minimum at (0,0,0). The animation should show progressively smaller steps as the gradient becomes smaller near the minimum.

11. Visualize the complete descent process
   plot z=x²+2y² together with (xₖ,yₖ,f(xₖ,yₖ))
   The final visualization should include the bowl-shaped surface, the current point, an arrow representing the negative gradient, and a connected sequence of points showing the descending path. The path should begin at (3,2), move downhill, and approach (0,0,0). The visual supports the calculation but does not replace the update computations.

12. State the final gradient-descent rule
   boxed (xₖ₊₁,yₖ₊₁)=(xₖ,yₖ)-ηbegin bmatrix2xₖ\\4yₖend bmatrix, η=0.1
   For the surface z=x^2+2y^2, gradient descent subtracts the learning-rate-scaled gradient (2x_k,4y_k) from the current point. Starting from (3,2), this rule generates the descending sequence and converges toward the minimum (0,0,0).

Answer: boxed (xₖ₊₁,yₖ₊₁)=(xₖ,yₖ)-ηbegin bmatrix2xₖ\\4yₖend bmatrix, η=0.1
For z=f(x,y)=x^2+2y^2, the gradient is ∇f(x,y)=(2x,4y), so the downhill direction is its negative. Gradient descent therefore updates the point by subtracting eta times this gradient. With the illustrative start (3,2) and eta=0.1, the first point is (2.4,1.2), followed by points approaching (0,0). The associated surface heights descend toward the minimum z=0 at (0,0,0).

12 steps, 12 slides — 6 step(s) sympy could not prove — 17% of slides draw a figure

operations.title: The Loss Surface

parameters.description: 3D surface z=x^2+2y^2 over x,y in [-3,3], with x and y base axes, vertical z axis labelled loss, and minimum marked at (0,0,0).

operations.caption: z=f(x,y)=x^2+2y^2
operations.narration: Think of the loss as height above the x-y plane. The surface z equals x squared plus 2y squared is a bowl, and its lowest point is at the origin.

operations.title: Choose a Starting Point

parameters.description: Retain the 3D bowl z=x^2+2y^2 over x,y in [-3,3]. Mark the surface point (3,2,22), label it current point (3,2), and project it vertically to (3,2,0).

operations.caption: (x_0,y_0)=(3,2)
operations.narration: To make the descent concrete, start at the surface point whose horizontal coordinates are x zero equals 3 and y zero equals 2.

operations.title: Measure the Slope
operations.caption: \nabla f(x,y)=\begin{bmatrix}2x\\4y\end{bmatrix}
operations.narration: The gradient collects the rate of change in the x direction and the rate of change in the y direction. Differentiating gives 2x and 4y.

operations.title: The Gradient Points Uphill
operations.caption: -\nabla f(x,y)=\begin{bmatrix}-2x\\-4y\end{bmatrix}
operations.narration: The gradient points in the direction where the loss rises fastest. To reduce the loss, we travel in the opposite direction.

operations.title: The Update Rule
operations.caption: (x_{k+1},y_{k+1})=(x_k,y_k)-\eta\nabla f(x_k,y_k)
operations.narration: At each step, multiply the gradient by the learning rate eta, then subtract that vector from the current coordinates. This produces the next point.

operations.title: First Downhill Step
operations.caption: (x_1,y_1)=(3-0.1(2\cdot3),\;2-0.1(4\cdot2))=(2.4,1.2)
operations.narration: At the starting coordinates, the gradient is 6 in x and 8 in y. With eta equal to 0.1, subtracting the scaled gradient moves the point to 2.4 comma 1.2.

operations.title: The x-Coordinate Shrinks
operations.caption: x:\;3,\;2.4,\;1.92,\;1.536,\;1.2288,\;0.98304
operations.narration: Repeating the x update gives 3, 2.4, 1.92, 1.536, 1.2288, and 0.98304. The x coordinate steadily moves toward zero.

operations.title: The y-Coordinate Shrinks Faster
operations.caption: y:\;2,\;1.2,\;0.72,\;0.432,\;0.2592,\;0.15552
operations.narration: The y sequence is 2, 1.2, 0.72, 0.432, 0.2592, and 0.15552. It contracts faster because the surface is steeper in the y direction.

operations.title: Every Step Lowers the Loss
operations.caption: f(x-0.1(2x),y-0.1(4y))=0.64x^2+0.72y^2
operations.narration: After one update, the loss becomes 0.64x squared plus 0.72y squared. Both coefficients are smaller than before, so every nonzero point loses height for this learning rate.

operations.title: Convergence to the Minimum
operations.caption: \lim_{k\to\infty}(x_k,y_k)=(0,0)
operations.narration: As the point gets closer to the bottom, the gradient gets smaller. The steps shrink, and the coordinates converge to zero.

operations.title: The Complete Descent

parameters.description: Show the complete 3D surface z=x^2+2y^2 over x,y in [-3,3], axes, start point (3,2,22), connected trajectory points with the verified sequences, negative-gradient arrows, and minimum (0,0,0) labelled z=0.

operations.caption: \text{plot }z=x^2+2y^2\text{ together with }(x_k,y_k,f(x_k,y_k))
operations.narration: The whole process is now visible: the path begins at (3,2), follows negative-gradient directions down the bowl, and approaches the minimum at the origin, where the loss is zero.

operations.title: FINAL ANSWER
operations.caption: \boxed{(x_{k+1},y_{k+1})=(x_k,y_k)-\eta\begin{bmatrix}2x_k\\4y_k\end{bmatrix},\qquad \eta=0.1}
operations.narration: The gradient-descent rule is the current point minus eta times the gradient. Here eta is 0.1, generating a descending sequence from (3,2) toward the minimum (0,0,0).
